significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that "early-layer prediction stability" predictively couples a token’s convergence layer to the causal dispensability of later computation, with an ordering in which "connective/filler/restating tokens" converge shallower than "genuine deduction tokens"; this is a form-(iii) relation rather than merely an existence or single-behavior steering claim. It establishes both a phenomenon—semantic reasoning roles have systematically different depth requirements—and a mechanism—late-layer contributions are unnecessary after convergence but remain behaviorally important for deep tokens—thereby predicting depth patterns and safe early-exit decisions on further CoT instances; this bears directly on the adaptive-computation decisions studied by CALM (Schuster et al., 2022), Mixture-of-Depths (Raposo et al., 2024), and LayerSkip (Elhoushi et al., 2024). The claim is determinate, and a negative result would meaningfully rule out logit-stability and the proposed semantic classes as reliable indicators of required computation, although it would not rule out other adaptive-depth signals. In the topic-substitution check, the generic topic of efficient interpretable reasoning would not itself justify this score; the score comes from the specific semantic ordering and convergence-to-causal-necessity coupling.

reach.justification: The named handles are the online "convergence layer," "early-layer prediction stability," and the resulting "training-free per-token depth-allocation controller" that skips remaining layers after stable convergence. This is ex ante within token computation: it fires before the expensive later layers and leaves an immediate action window, making it useful to inference-system builders rather than only to researchers performing post-hoc attribution. Although thresholds may need re-extraction or calibration, the asserted relation predicts that shallow convergence will again indicate safe skipping and that semantic token roles will preserve a depth ordering; its stated scope is transformer CoT reasoning across tasks and open-weight model families, not other modalities or arbitrary architectures. The topic-substitution check does not preserve the score: without this particular predictor and intervention, the broad efficient-reasoning topic supplies no comparable transferable handle.
